chunks: Ibn Abī ʿUmayr narrated from Murāzim, from ʿAmmār al-Sābāṭī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
The deceased has the greatest right to his wealth so long as the soul remains in him and he is able to express himself by it.
He عليه السلام said: But if he exceeds, then he is entitled only to one-third.

key_terms.الثُّلُثُ: one-third, the legal limit of bequest beyond heirs' shares
key_terms.الرُّوحُ: the soul, meaning while life still remains
key_terms.الْمَيِّتُ: the dying person or deceased person in the context of testamentary rights
key_terms.يُبِينُ بِهِ: able to make his intention clear and express it

ai.seo_question: How much of a person's wealth can be disposed of in a bequest according to Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith states that a person retains authority over his wealth while alive and able to express his wishes. However, if he exceeds the proper limit in his bequest, then only one-third is valid. It is a foundational narration in Shia fiqh on the limits of testamentary disposal.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.5426 - Ibn Abi Umayr narrated from Murazim from Ammar Al-Sabaṭi from Abu Abdullah Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as), who said:
"The deceased has the most right over his wealth as long as his soul remains in him and he can express himself."
Imam (as) then said: "But if he exceeds (in his bequest), he is entitled only to one-third."
